switchLang: Language: {lang}. Click for the next one (the studio only).
importReplace: A creation is already named {name}. Replace it? Its animations will be lost.
noModelsDir: Choose the models folder of {game} in the settings.
noModels: No entity here: only the living entities of the game (characters, creatures, enemies) are listed.
noCreations: Nothing yet: what you change in a model is saved here, the original is never touched.
pickModel: Pick an entity on the left to see it and play its animations.
twinAnimations: Add {n} animations from models with the same skeleton
gameAnimations: These {n} animations are the game's (Jak and Daxter are in every level): only those you add are checked and exported.
tryStep_compiler: Starting the game's compiler (a minute or two the first time)
tryStep_load: Taking Jak to the test level
inGame: In the game: the animation picked here plays there too. One the game does not hold yet, or one you edit, is built again (the game restarts).
guideUsageIntro: What the studio does, from finding a model to seeing it in the game. The second tab puts a model in a mod of yours, step by step.
useBrowseText: The list on the left holds the game's living entities (characters, creatures, enemies) and your creations, the copies the studio keeps of what you change. Pick one to open it.
useLooksText: The model as the game's code draws it. Nothing here changes the model or its textures: the studio only edits animations.
useNewText: New animation puts a movement on the model: from a video of one person, a motion capture file (BVH, FBX, glTF), or by hand. It is saved in the model's creation: the original model never changes.
useKeysText: The clapperboard next to an animation opens its keys: pick a joint, turn or move it, and a key is set at the moment shown. K keys a joint as it is, Del deletes its key, Ctrl+Z undoes.
useCheckText: Game check lists what build-actor would stop on or build wrong. Export writes the creation as build-actor needs it, with a README of the lines to add to the game. Jak's and Daxter's own animations are the game's: only those you add are checked and exported.
useTryText: Try in the game builds the model into the game's test level and starts the game: the model plays the animation picked, and the next one you pick. The game's files are put back when it closes.
useSettingsText: The folders the studio works with, the language, and the AI assistant.
useMcpText: Settings give the command that adds the studio's MCP server to Claude Code. The assistant then lists the models, makes animations from your words or from a motion capture, and checks them in the game; the studio shows what it does.
useLogText: Every error is written to errors.log in the studio's folder; the try in the game writes what goalc and the game said to game-test/<game>/goalc.log and gk.log there.
useWatchText: The model plays its first animation in the view; the bar under the view drives it.
useAnimsText: The right panel lists the model's animations: click one to play it. The buttons of a line show when the mouse is over it.
ctl_games: The game whose models are listed.
ctl_tabs: The game's entities, or your creations: the copies the studio keeps of the models you changed (the original never changes).
ctl_search: Finds an entity by its official name or its file's.
ctl_refresh: Reads the list again: a creation the AI assistant made, or a new extraction of the game.
ctl_import: Copies .glb files of your own into the creations.
ctl_variants: An entity the game splits into several models (high detail, in a vehicle...): the arrow opens them.
ctl_timeBar: Drags the animation to a moment; each mark above it is a key, the orange ones the picked joint's.
ctl_skeleton: Shows the joints and bones over the model.
ctl_view: Drag to turn around the model, right-drag to move, wheel to zoom.
ctl_badge: Original: the game's model, read only. Creation: your copy, the one exported.
ctl_folder: Opens the folder of the model's file.
ctl_gameTag: Jak's or Daxter's own animation: the game has it, so it is neither checked nor exported; it can be tried in the game, and edited into a version of your own.
ctl_editKeys: Opens the animation in the key editor.
ctl_twins: Adds the animations other files of the same entity and skeleton hold, where the extraction put them.
ctl_new: Makes a new animation from a video, a motion capture file or by hand.
ctl_forms: Jak as himself, as Dark Jak (shapes, skin, black eyes) or as Light Jak (the game's lights).
ctl_wings: Light Jak's wings, out only when he glides.
ctl_gun: Puts the Morph Gun in Jak's hand, with the mod of your choice.
ctl_armor: Shows or hides the armor pieces of a model without the game's segments.
ctl_outfit: Every look the game's code gives the model (colours, hats, weapons...); Random picks one.
ctl_segments: The model's pieces one by one, to show or hide.
ctl_shapes: The blend shapes (Dark Jak's, Jak's goggles and scarf), from 0 to 1.
ctl_source: Where the movement comes from: a video of one person, a BVH, FBX or glTF file, or nothing (the rest pose, to key by hand).
ctl_fps: How many keys the animation gets a second: 15 by default, as the game's own animations; more is finer, and heavier.
ctl_extract: Reads the movement and puts it on the model, next to the orange figure of the capture.
ctl_face: Turns the movement to face the model's front.
ctl_inPlace: Keeps the model on the spot, as the game wants: its code moves it through the level.
ctl_hold: Keeps a weapon in both hands, with the arms of the model's first animation.
ctl_mapping: Which joint of the model plays which body part.
ctl_refine: Goes on in the key editor.
ctl_save: Saves the animation in the model's creation.
ctl_duration: How long the animation lasts, in seconds.
ctl_joint: The joint to move; clicking its dot in the view picks it too.
ctl_tools: Turns the joint with its rings, or moves it with its arrows: a key is set at the moment shown.
ctl_steps: Goes to the previous or next key.
ctl_addKey: Keys the joint as it is, at the moment shown.
ctl_deleteKey: Deletes the joint's key at the moment shown.
ctl_rest: Puts the joint back to its rest pose at the moment shown.
ctl_saveKeys: Saves the animation; with the game of a try open, the studio builds it again with your version.
ctl_check: What build-actor would stop on (red) or what is worth knowing (yellow), animation by animation.
ctl_export: Writes the creation as build-actor needs it, with a README of the lines to add to the game.
ctl_try: Shows the model in the game's test level, playing the animation picked. Greyed out, with the reason under it, when the game cannot be started: no installation, another game open, Jak and Daxter.
ctl_close: Closes the game; its own files are put back.
ctl_modelsDirs: Each game's models, the decompiler's decompiler_out/<game>/levels folder. Read only.
ctl_creationsDir: Where the studio keeps your creations.
ctl_gameDir: Each game's installation: the OpenGOAL Launcher's folder, an OpenGOAL release or a jak-project. The game the studio tries models in, and where exports go.
ctl_language: English or French; the button with the language’s code in the title bar (EN, FR) switches it too, for the studio only.
ctl_mcp: The command that adds the studio's MCP server to Claude Code.
guideUseOpened: Make the lines for the model opened: {model}
guideTitle: Put a model in the game
guideIntro: These steps put {model} in {game}''s test level as an entity of its own, which plays its animations. Every line is made for this model, the one last opened in the studio.
guideIntroExample: These steps put a model in the game's test level as an entity of its own, which plays its animations. The example is Jak 3's Marauder, with a wave made in the studio.
guideNeed: You need a jak-project where {game} builds, and the model exported with Export for {game}. The studio's Try in the game does all of this in a copy of the test level: these steps are for your own mod.
guideModelText: Copy the export's custom_assets folder into your jak-project: the model lands here. With the game's installation folder set in the settings, the export already put it there.
guideBuildText: In goal_src/{gameId}/game.gp, next to the other build-actor lines: the art group holds the model's skeleton and animations.
guideMesh: Put its mesh in the level
guideMeshText: In {level}/test-zone.jsonc, add the model to the list custom_models: the level's file holds its mesh.
guideCodeText: A new file, goal_src/{gameId}/levels/test-zone/{type}.gc. def-actor names the animations in the file's order: each symbol is a slot of the art group. The entity loops on its first animation, and plays {anim} once when it gets the event ''{event}.
guideCompileText: In goal_src/{gameId}/game.gp: the code becomes an object file, {type}.o.
guideLoadText: In {level}/testzone.gd, the level's list of files: the entity's code first, the art group before the level's own file (the lines already there stay in place of ...).
guidePlace: Place the entity in the level
guidePlaceText: In {level}/test-zone.jsonc, add it to the list actors: its etype is the entity's type, its name the one the code finds it by, trans its place in metres.
guidePlayText: In goalc: build the game with (mi), start it, connect with (lt), go to the test level, then send the event: the entity plays {anim}.
guideNotBornText: A level made by hand has no visibility data: with the game's PS2 actor visibility on (PS2 actor vis in the debug menu), its entities are never born. Turn it off, or in goalc:
guideMemory: Every animation takes the game's memory
guideMemoryText: A level loads each of its files, the art group whole, into a buffer of 2 MB in Jak and Daxter, 1 750 KB in Jak II and Jak 3, and checks nothing: a bigger art group writes over the memory after it, and the game crashes. Game check gives its size once built: keep the animations your entity plays. Past that, the game itself has to change, probably a mod of yours: the dgo-level-buf-2 buffers of goal_src/{gameId}/engine/level/level.gc, and the level's heap they come from (LEVEL_HEAP_SIZE).
guideJak1: Jak and Daxter closes when a level loads an entity with a skeleton added this way (jak-project of October 2026): try your models in Jak II or Jak 3.
looksHint: The model's variants, as the game's code draws them: Outfit picks one, the lists show or hide its parts. What is shown here never changes the model: the studio only edits animations.
segments: {n} segments (as the game turns them on)
noWings: {name}.glb is not in the model's folder nor in the game's models folder.
noGameTextures: The eyes and Dark Jak's skin are drawn from the game's textures (decompiler_out/<game>/textures), next to the models folder or in the game's installation folder of the settings.
manualHint: Pose the joints yourself with the mouse, key by key, from the rest pose.
editorHint: Click a joint (a dot in the view) and turn it with its rings: a key is set at the time shown. Move along the time bar and pose it again: the game blends from key to key.
addKey: Key the joint as it is (K)
restPose: Back to the rest pose here
videoHint: A video of one person, whole body in view. The first time, the pose model (about 9 MB) is downloaded.
mocapHint: BVH, FBX or glTF with an animated skeleton (Mixamo, CMU...).
name: Name
fpsHint: The game's own animations have 15 keys a second. More keeps finer detail of the movement in a heavier file; in the game, an animation's size depends on its length and on the joints that move (build-actor makes 60 frames a second whatever the keys).
inPlaceHint: Unticked: the model travels during the animation, then goes back to its start at each loop.
modelsDirHint: For each game, the .glb files of its entities (models with an armature). They are only read.
creationsDirHint: Each model you change is copied here with its animations, ready to export.
gameDirHint: Where the game is installed: the studio tries models in it when started on its own (from the OpenGOAL Launcher, it uses the Launcher's games), and exports go into its custom_assets folder. Expected folders, for example:
gameDirLauncher: the OpenGOAL Launcher's installation folder, the one that holds active: C:\Games\OpenGOAL
gameDirRelease: an OpenGOAL release unzipped, the folder that holds gk.exe: C:\Games\opengoal-v0.3.9
gameDirProject: a jak-project built with its game, your mod's: C:\dev\jak-project
mcpHint: Lets Claude Code, or any MCP client, define game-ready animations. Register it once:
welcome: Choose the models folder of a game to start.
noBody: {file}: no body was found in the video.
tryNoAnimation: Pick the animation to try in the game.
holdWeaponHint: The arms keep the pose of the model's first animation, the weapon in both hands; the rest of the body follows the capture. Unticked: the arms follow the capture, the weapon the hand holding it.
noBodyMocap: {file}: none of its bones was recognised as hips and legs (by their names).
notMocap: {file}: a motion capture file is a .bvh, .fbx, .glb or .gltf.
core_no-skin: The model has no armature (skin): it is not an entity.
core_several-skins: The model has {count} armatures (skins), build-actor takes one.
core_joint-order: Joint ''{joint}'' comes before its parent in the armature: build-actor needs every parent first.
core_joint-child: Joint ''{joint}'' has a child that is not a joint (''{child}''): build-actor stops on it. Parent that object to the armature instead.
core_no-align: The first joint is not 'align': build-actor adds one, so the game's joint numbers are one more than the file's, and 'align' (which moves the entity in game) cannot be animated.
core_align-origin: Joint 'align' is not at the origin.
core_too-many-joints: The armature has {count} joints, build-actor takes {max} at most.
core_too-few-joints: build-actor needs at least two joints.
core_skin-joints: {outside} vertex weights go to joints the armature does not have (up to joint {highest}, it has {joints}): build-actor passes them on, and the game moves them with other joints.
core_model-name: The game names the art group after the file: ''{suggested}'' would be safer than ''{name}'' (lowercase, digits and dashes).
core_no-animation: The model has no animation: build-actor makes a still pose of it.
core_weights: It has morph target (weights) keys on {target}: build-actor stops on them. Export removes them.
core_not-a-joint: It moves node {target}, which is not a joint of the armature: build-actor stops on it. Export drops these keys.
core_cubic-spline: Its keys on {target} are cubic splines: build-actor reads linear keys only. Export makes them linear.
core_step: Its keys on {target} are steps: the game blends between them.
core_keys: Its keys on {target} cannot be read: {error}.
core_starts-late: Its keys on {target} start at {time} s: the game starts at 0.
core_missing-keys: {count} joint channels have no keys ({list}): the game puts them at the origin instead of their rest pose. Export gives them their rest pose.
core_frame-too-big: One frame takes {bytes} bytes, build-actor allows {max}: move fewer joints (a channel whose keys never change costs nothing per frame).
core_fixed-too-big: Its constant part takes {bytes} bytes, build-actor allows {max}.
core_node-dropped: {anim}: keys of node {node} (not a joint) dropped
core_rest-keyed: {anim}: joints without keys keyed at their rest pose
core_still-pose-held: {anim}: a still pose, given a second key 1/60 s later (build-actor stops on it otherwise)
core_no-game-folder: Choose the game's installation folder in the settings, or start the studio from the OpenGOAL Launcher.
core_game-not-in-launcher: This game is not installed with the OpenGOAL Launcher's active tooling ({version}): install or update it in the Launcher.
core_game-not-found: {folder} holds no game to try in: choose an OpenGOAL Launcher installation, an OpenGOAL release or a jak-project with the game built.
core_game-incomplete: The game in {folder} lacks {file}: install or build it again.
core_game-port-taken: Another game listens on port {port}: close it first.
core_game-closed: The game closed during the try: {output}
core_game-not-playing: The game does not play {anim}: the art group's element {slot} is another animation.
core_try-jak1: Jak and Daxter closes when a level loads a character added this way: try models in Jak II or Jak 3.
core_art-group-too-big: The model takes {size} KB once built, more than the {max} KB a level of the game loads it into: remove or shorten animations.
core_animations-too-big: The animations take {size} KB once built, the mesh not counted: more than a level of any game loads an art group into (2048 KB in Jak and Daxter, 1750 KB in Jak II and Jak 3). Remove or shorten animations.
core_animations-too-big-23: The animations take {size} KB once built, the mesh not counted: more than a level of Jak II or Jak 3 loads an art group into (1750 KB; 2048 KB in Jak and Daxter). Remove or shorten animations for those games.
core_not-an-entity: {file} is not an entity: an entity has one armature (skin).
core_game-name-shared: In the game, ''{anim}'' would be named {name}, as ''{other}'' is: give it another name.
